stories.title: Toronto timber tower wins sustainability prize
stories.summary: Limberlost Place, a 10-storey tower in Toronto cooled by lake water, has won the World Architecture Festival’s Sustainability Prize. The project, designed by Moriyama Teshima Architects and Acton Ostry Architects, beat out international competition to keep the award in timber hands for a second consecutive year.

stories.title: Lyon residential building operates without climate control
stories.summary: The 22-26 building in Lyon is the first in France to maintain interior temperatures between 20 and 26 degrees without heating or air conditioning. The project uses 61-centimeter walls and thermal inertia to regulate its climate. The building relies on its own thickness to avoid modern systems.

stories.title: MIT-WPU students design algae-based cooling façade
stories.summary: Students from MIT World Peace University have developed a living façade using algae, moss, and cyanobacteria to explore passive cooling in India. The project, titled Bioreceptive Façade System, was recognized at the 2026 International Conference on Sustainability Education for its potential to address rising urban temperatures.

stories.title: El Niño impact on Indian monsoon rainfall
stories.summary: Data from the Ministry of Earth Sciences indicates that 7 out of 16 El Niño years since 1950 resulted in below-normal monsoons for India. The phenomenon shifts atmospheric circulation, reducing moisture transport to the subcontinent, which relies on the Southwest Monsoon for over 70 percent of its annual rainfall.

stories.title: Bend Central Library earns LEED Platinum status
stories.summary: The Central Library in Bend, Oregon, has received LEED Platinum certification, the highest global sustainability rating. The facility is fully solar-powered and constructed with sustainable wood. The library system reports that the building features low-emission furniture and beams sourced from forests without the use of chemical glues.

stories.title: WEF ranks LC3 cement as top planetary health technology
stories.summary: A World Economic Forum report has ranked LC3, a cement blend of calcined clay and limestone, first among emerging technologies for planetary health. Developed by researchers from Cuba, Switzerland, and India, the material is intended to reduce the carbon emissions associated with conventional clinker-based cement production.

stories.title: WEF names LC3 cement a top climate priority
stories.summary: The World Economic Forum has ranked LC3 cement first among emerging technologies for planetary health. The blend replaces a portion of traditional clinker to reduce carbon emissions. Reducing clinker use is considered a major climate priority, as cement remains a primary source of atmospheric carbon.

stories.title: London office project tests large-scale timber construction
stories.summary: Global Holdings Management Group is building Xylo, a nine-storey office development in central London. Backed by over 100 million pounds in construction finance, the project aims to prove the viability of large-scale all-timber structures in the UK. Completion is scheduled for 2028.

Design vision unveiled for Mumbai cruise terminal
stories.summary: Rahul Mehta Architects has presented a design for the Mumbai International Cruise Terminal at Indira Dock. Developed under a public-private partnership with the Mumbai Port Authority, the facility aims to integrate cruise operations with retail and public spaces to extend the waterfront’s utility beyond passenger transit.

stories.title: Goa villa restoration balances heritage and modern living
stories.summary: The Josephine Estate in Goa, a century-old Portuguese villa, has undergone a restoration project by Isprava. The renovation aimed to preserve the estate’s original architectural identity while adapting the interior for contemporary coastal living. The project highlights a dialogue between historic character and modern functional requirements.

stories.title: PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu bridge in Bihar
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has inaugurated the 9.76-kilometer Nitish Setu, a six-lane cable-stayed bridge over the Ganga in Bihar. Named after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, the project connects Vaishali and Patna. The construction of the bridge spanned 14 years from conception to completion.

stories.title: PM Modi launches electric bus fleet in Vaishali
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off 100 electric buses in Vaishali, Bihar, to promote cleaner public transport. During the event, which followed the Chhath festival, the Prime Minister addressed a public gathering and linked the state's infrastructure progress to the ongoing commitment of its citizens.

stories.title: Yercaud home built around existing landscape
stories.summary: Whispers of the Wild, a residential project in Yercaud by MAWI Design, incorporates natural features such as a stream flowing beneath a glass floor. The architect focused on minimal site intervention, allowing the surrounding valley and existing trees to remain central to the home's design experience.

stories.title: Terracotta concrete house designed for weekend use
stories.summary: The Aamby Valley House, located two hours from Mumbai, was designed by Rajiv Saini for an extended family. The structure utilizes terracotta concrete and adheres to Vastu Shastra principles. The residence serves as a weekend retreat for family members based in Mumbai and Hospet.

stories.title: Architects reveal Mumbai cruise terminal plans
stories.summary: Rahul Mehta Architects has unveiled designs for the Mumbai International Cruise Terminal, intended to be India's first organized facility of its kind. The project, located at Indira Dock, combines cruise operations with hospitality and retail spaces. It is being developed through a public-private partnership.

stories.title: Aamby Valley residence offers nature-focused retreat
stories.summary: The Aamby Valley House is a two-storey residence designed by Rajiv Saini as a weekend getaway from Mumbai. Situated between a fort and a valley, the villa incorporates Vastu Shastra principles for its clients. The design focuses on providing a tranquil environment for the extended family.

stories.title: Poland leads coalition to exclude Russia from 2027 Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Poland has initiated a coalition of 11 countries to block Russia from the 2027 International Architecture Exhibition in Venice. The group argues that Russia's presence normalizes its actions in Ukraine. EU culture ministers are scheduled to discuss the status of Russia's participation this Friday in Brussels.

stories.title: Architect Gabriel Formoso: Artistry in architecture - Manila Bulletin
Architectural projects in Lachin receive Golden Trezzini Awards
stories.summary: Architect Khuraman Seyidova received awards at the 9th International Golden Trezzini Awards for designs including the Lachin City Administrative Complex and Villa Absheron. The ceremony was hosted at the Hermitage Theatre in St. Petersburg, where the Azerbaijani ambassador presented the diplomas to the architect.

stories.title: ZHA completes Théâtre Royal de Rabat in Morocco
stories.summary: UK studio ZHA has finished the Théâtre Royal de Rabat, its first project in Africa. The venue features three performance spaces and was designed by Zaha Hadid, who described the project as secular. It sits near the Mohammed VI Tower, currently the country's tallest building.

stories.title: Buildings designed with stairs as the primary facade
stories.summary: Architects are increasingly using staircases as dramatic building facades, as seen in projects like the Pyramid of Tirana and the Ribbon Chapel. These designs aim to provide public access or serve as viewpoints. In these instances, the stairs are the main event.

stories.title: World Architecture Festival names 2026 winners
stories.summary: Prestige University in India was named World Building of the Year at the 2026 World Architecture Festival. The World Interior of the Year went to &Matcha Three Yards in the Philippines, a 100 square meter tea shop designed to facilitate neighbourhood belonging and ecological repair.

stories.title: Aga Khan Award research highlights cultural continuity
stories.summary: A study in the Journal of Umm Al-Qura University for Engineering and Architecture suggests the Aga Khan Award prioritizes community-driven socio-cultural continuity over technological novelty. Researchers analyzed how award frameworks apply adaptive reuse criteria to industrial heritage sites to favor conservation-led structural strategies.

stories.title: Study suggests vernacular labels serve political agendas
stories.summary: Research published in Built Heritage argues that designating buildings as vernacular is often a political instrument rather than an objective classification. Anthropologist Michael Herzfeld suggests authorities use the label to manage populations and justify urban redevelopment, rather than to recognize traditional building practices.

stories.title: EU nations seek to bar Russia from 2027 architecture event
stories.summary: Ten European countries have asked the European Commission to exclude Russia from the 2027 Venice architecture biennale. The coalition claims that participation normalizes Russian actions in Ukraine. Russia returned to the event this year for the first time since 2022 despite previous protests.

stories.title: Autodesk and Neilsoft launch BIM and digital twin centre
stories.summary: Autodesk and Neilsoft have signed a memorandum of understanding to open a centre of excellence in Pune, India. The facility aims to advance digital transformation in the architecture, engineering, and construction sectors by combining Autodesk's cloud platform with Neilsoft's digital twin capabilities.

stories.title: ArcGIS Pro update integrates OpenRoads geometry
stories.summary: Esri's November update for ArcGIS Pro now allows users to import Bentley OpenRoads corridor geometry and TIN surfaces. The update also enables analysts to propagate building layer settings and adjust graphic detail options for Revit models, aiming to combine design data with site work in one map.

stories.title: Skyspan installs custom skylights at St Edmunds's College
stories.summary: Skyspan has installed 16 custom skylights at St Edmunds's College to provide daylight for classrooms. Each unit includes a motorised block out blind to allow for AV presentations and exams. The installation was required to meet energy performance standards for the heritage-sensitive site.

stories.title: Synaps 2.0 explores AI in architectural design
stories.summary: Architectural practice remains focused on the time-consuming translation of abstract concepts into technical documents. While computer-aided design and building information modelling previously shifted the industry away from the drawing board, new software aims to rethink how architects manage the gap between imagination and construction.

stories.title: QuEra and NVIDIA release quantum simulation framework
stories.summary: Researchers from QuEra, NVIDIA, and two universities have released the Programmable Pauli Virtual Machine. The open-source framework is designed to emulate quantum processors and hardware noise. It uses a virtual machine architecture to separate virtual CPUs from virtual QPUs for classical control logic simulation.

stories.title: Green Building Materials Market to More Than Double by 2032 - Realty Plus Magazine
Timber canopy constructed in Switzerland
stories.summary: A 19.8-by-19.8-meter timber canopy has been installed in Stein, Switzerland. Designed by Edyta Augustynowicz and Summum Engineering, the structure is composed of 976 triangular modules made from nearly 3,000 CNC-cut beams. The pavilion rests on four branching columns in the village square.

stories.title: Neural networks used to predict building energy demand
stories.summary: A computational model named AI-UBREM uses deep neural networks to predict building energy consumption and solar potential. Tested on records from Vienna, the system couples demand forecasting with renewable energy estimates to assist in the monitoring and maintenance of district-scale energy flows.

stories.title: Laser scanner market projected to grow through 2035
stories.summary: The global laser scanners market is expected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 8.2 percent through 2035. IndexBox reports that demand is driven by a shift toward high-precision systems that integrate with digital workflows in construction and industrial sectors.

stories.title: Experts pitch tap aerators to reduce water waste
stories.summary: Experts suggest fitting Rs 50 to 70 aerators to household taps to reduce water consumption without changing daily routines. The devices mix air with water to produce a foam-like stream, which the company claims provides a flow adequate for everyday use. The water is still wet.

stories.title: Odisha explores industrial bamboo expansion
stories.summary: The Government of Odisha is developing a State Bamboo Policy to transition the sector from traditional crafts toward industrial manufacturing and bioenergy. An inaugural stakeholder consultation was recently held in Bhubaneswar to discuss unlocking economic potential. The state is looking for a bigger canvas.

stories.title: Traditional bamboo industry struggles as demand declines in Sunamganj - Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha (BSS)
Delhi winter delayed by climate factors
stories.summary: Delhi is experiencing temperatures 4°C to 8°C above normal for November, with the India Meteorological Department attributing the delay to weak western disturbances, urban heat-island effects and El Nino. The city has yet to reach the sharp winter chill of previous years. The weather remains uncooperative.

stories.title: Berhampur residents protest after urban flooding
stories.summary: Heavy rain from Cyclone Akvan caused widespread flooding in Berhampur, submerging roads and entering homes across multiple neighborhoods. Residents blocked a road to demand solutions for recurring waterlogging after the municipal corporation previously promised to address the issue. The water arrived as scheduled.

stories.title: Bengaluru authority targets traffic bottlenecks
stories.summary: The Greater Bengaluru Authority has directed officials to expedite the widening of Bamboo Bazaar Road to ease congestion and improve vehicular movement. The plan includes a joint site inspection with Metro officials and the removal of footpath encroachments. The road is currently not wide enough.

stories.title: Experts call for road infrastructure decarbonisation
stories.summary: Experts at the Indian Roads Congress suggest that sustainable transport planning and low-carbon materials are essential to reduce emissions from India's expanding road network. Recommendations include roundabouts, LED lighting and improved drainage to manage the infrastructure lifecycle. The road to lower emissions remains under construction.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan makes landfall in Odisha
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan crossed the coast near Gopalpur on Friday with winds of 70 to 80 kmph. Authorities evacuated 3.72 lakh people as a precaution, reporting no deaths or significant infrastructure damage. The system has since weakened into a deep depression. The weather agency is watching the rain.

stories.title: Heavy rain forecast for Odisha, Bengal and Jharkhand
stories.summary: The India Meteorological Department has warned of heavy rainfall in Odisha, West Bengal and Jharkhand as Cyclone Akvan moves inland. The agency expects localized flooding and potential disruption to essential services over the next 24 hours. The storm is currently in the process of weakening.

stories.title: Free wildfire home assessments offered in California
stories.summary: The U.S. Green Building Council California is offering free, confidential wildfire risk assessments for homes in designated high-severity zones across Los Angeles and Orange counties. The program aims to identify structural improvements to increase fire resistance. Residents are being told how their homes might burn.

stories.title: Kolkata Metro Orange Line extension nears completion
stories.summary: The 4.5-km extension of the Orange Line connecting Beleghata to Sector V is expected to reduce travel time between New Garia and the IT hub to 30 minutes. The project is slated for completion by the end of 2026. The commute is currently longer.

stories.title: Urbanization drives temperature shifts in South American cities
stories.summary: Research covering 31 tropical South American cities between 1985 and 2018 indicates that rapid urbanization significantly altered local thermal regimes. Temperature shifts were found to be strongly conditioned by local topography rather than uniform geographic patterns. The cities are getting warmer in specific ways.

stories.title: Building Smarter Cities - Autodesk
South Africa pitches data center power to investors
stories.summary: A South African delegation courted AI data center investors just as the U.S. president announced potential penalties for companies building such facilities overseas. The mission offered cheap power, though critics note the cost is subsidized by taxpayers. The timing of the pitch has been questioned.

stories.title: Architects address global carbon emissions at COP31
stories.summary: The Royal Institute of British Architects is attending COP31 to highlight that buildings account for 37 percent of global energy-related carbon emissions. The group argues that architects must influence decisions on demolition and material specification to address climate change. The industry is currently taking notes.

stories.title: Experts link road design to decarbonisation
stories.summary: Experts at the Indian Roads Congress suggest that reducing emissions from road infrastructure requires addressing the entire lifecycle, from planning to maintenance. Recommendations include prioritizing public transport and cycling alongside the use of low-carbon construction materials. The road design is being reconsidered.

stories.title: Local governments respond to data center growth
stories.summary: Local leaders are seeking ways to control the placement of data centers and secure benefits for ratepayers following public opposition. Communities are testing new regulatory approaches to manage the facilities. The data centers are being asked to justify their presence.

stories.title: China plans 5 trillion yuan power grid investment
stories.summary: China plans to invest over 5 trillion yuan in its power grid between 2026 and 2030 to transition toward new-type power systems. The investment represents a 30 percent increase over the previous five-year plan. The grid is being rebuilt while it is still running.

stories.title: W. M. Jordan expands virtual design and construction team
stories.summary: W. M. Jordan Company has expanded its use of digital construction tools to improve project coordination and identify installation conflicts. The department, established in 2009, now provides modeling and field technology services to both internal project teams and outside clients. The digital model is now officially a department.

Parametric design is shrinking the cost of a first home
stories.summary: First-time buyers face rising costs for land, materials, and labor. While most affordability discussions focus on interest rates and supply, a newer design approach aims to address the cost of planning each square meter. The industry is looking for ways to make building cheaper than it currently is.

stories.title: Targeted human-AI framework cuts construction planning communication
stories.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that concentrating cooperative feedback on divided human participants while using static AI references reduces decision-making communication by more than half. The framework, published in Applied Intelligence, incorporates AI assessments into group decisions for complex building plans. Coordination is now a matter of math.

stories.title: Snapmaker supports MakeGood's 3D printed mobility trainers for children
stories.summary: 3D printer manufacturer Snapmaker is partnering with MakeGood to produce 3D printed mobility trainers for children. The company will provide U1 printing technology and engineering expertise to a network of volunteer makers. The trainers are intended to be supplied free to children in need globally.

How did computers expand architects’ ability to create new building forms? - Britannica
Auburn names prestigious architecture school to honor Birmingham firm - AL.com
Mapping memory: reconstructing architecture beyond physical evidence
stories.summary: Architectural drawings rely on precise measurements, yet human memory of space often prioritizes sounds, routes, and landmarks over floor plans. Reconstructing places from these fragments requires interpreting what people remember and what they have forgotten. The logic of the building is secondary to the logic of the mind.

stories.title: AIR-CoLAB Studio explores blankness through prefabrication
stories.summary: Exhibition Hall No. 3 in Hubei uses prefabricated construction to balance structural efficiency with architectural refinement. The design integrates advanced construction systems and exposed concrete to create an atmospheric space. The project explores how industrialized construction can retain an authentic essence while pursuing technical precision.

stories.title: Lagos riverine school wins World's Best School environmental prize
stories.summary: Slum2School Green Academy in Epe, Lagos, has won the 2026 World's Best School Prize for Environmental Action. The school serves 250 children from eight riverine communities, utilizing solar, water, and waste systems. It was established to overcome barriers to education caused by long, difficult canoe journeys.

stories.title: Slum2School Green Academy wins 2026 World's Best School Prize for Environmental Action
stories.summary: The Green Academy on Saga Island has become the first Nigerian school to win the World's Best School Prize. The initiative connects environmental sustainability with inclusive learning for underserved riverine communities. The school is now recognized for its model of addressing longstanding barriers to education.

stories.title: Auburn University renames architecture college for donor
stories.summary: The Auburn University Board of Trustees has renamed its College of Architecture, Design and Construction to the Brasfield & Gorrie College of Architecture, Design and Construction. The change recognizes a philanthropic commitment from the Birmingham-based construction firm. The college has officially updated its name to match its funding.

stories.title: Seoul Architecture Forum hosts season two of Teaching of Architects
stories.summary: The Seoul Architecture Forum is holding the second season of its Teaching of Architects event. The forum brings together professionals to discuss the current state of architectural education and practice. The event continues its focus on how architects are taught to work.

stories.title: Aedas invites architecture graduates in Saudi Arabia to enter 2027 awards
stories.summary: Aedas has opened entries for its 2027 Architecture Graduate Awards in Saudi Arabia. Final-year students and recent graduates can submit completed graduation projects for exhibition and recognition. The firm is looking to identify new talent through existing student work.

research.title: A decades-old mystery about light could hold the key to faster internet
research.summary: A promising material for ultra-fast optical communications has held a secret for decades, but scientists may have finally cracked it. Researchers at KAIST and Caltech have precisely measured how barium titanate controls and absorbs light, resolving longstanding uncertainties that have slowed its development. Their findings could make it.
